A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local intrinsic-dimension framework. Their text, equations, figures, table, and appendices A–C are readable and support matching retained, expanded, and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning, arithmetic grokking, dialogue state tracking, and emotion-recognition experiments, together with sampling and noise analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds model/domain evaluations and quantitative correlation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain sequence sampling, embedding deduplication, token sampling, neighborhood construction, local TwoNN estimation, and aggregation. LoRA is introduced for additional evaluation models, without changing the proposed diagnostic procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds ICLR 2024 submission titles and abstracts as a scholarly-text evaluation domain, with results in Figures 12–14 and dataset sizes in Table 1. The original dialogue, Reddit, Wikipedia, emotion-recognition, and modular-arithmetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: No competing diagnostic or intrinsic-dimension estimator is added or removed. Comparisons with loss, task-performance metrics, and global TwoNN remain. The additional language models and fine-tuned variants are experimental configurations to which the same diagnostic is applied.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 substantially extends evaluation configurations to Phi-3.5-mini-instruct and Llama-3.1-8B, with 3.82B/8.03B parameters and 3072/4096-dimensional embeddings. These models use rank-16 LoRA on 10,000 sampled sequences and are evaluated after 800 batches. Additional fine-tuning configurations and Spearman correlation metrics are introduced; existing experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 add quantitative association analyses connecting local dimension with grokking accuracy, dialogue state tracking performance, and emotion-recognition loss. The sampling, neighborhood-size, noise, masking, layer-wise, individual-seed, and longer-training analyses already present in v1 are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Spearman rank-correlation estimation, including correlations calculated after step-wise averaging over six seeds in Section 4.3. Existing seed counts, grokking confidence intervals, and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Figures 11–14 substantially expand the reported model-by-corpus results while retaining matched earlier values. New entries include Llama-3.1-8B MultiWOZ mean dimensions of 8.26 for the base model and 6.56 after MultiWOZ fine-tuning. Section 4.3 adds dimension–JGA correlations of −0.982/−0.958/−0.905 across training/validation/test. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The embedding-space definitions, local TwoNN construction, distributional assumptions, and computational-complexity discussion remain substantively unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added. The new dimensionality hypothesis is interpretive rather than mathematical.

C1.justification: V2 partially narrows predictive claims: the introduction changes training-convergence prediction to indication, Section 4.2 changes grokking prediction to detection, and the conclusion says dimensionality reductions suggest improved generalization. The abstract still retains predictive language, and the central contributions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 adds a hypothesis of an intermediate dimensionality 'sweet spot,' with very low dimension potentially indicating over-compression or memorization, and explicitly leaves causality unresolved. Section 4.4 also clarifies why validation loss is a suitable stopping signal for emotion recognition but can mislead for dialogue state tracking.

D1.justification: V2 supplies two code-repository links absent from v1. It also documents the added models' dimensions, LoRA rank, sample sizes, checkpoint selection, and ICLR dataset split sizes. Existing implementation, hardware, and timing information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lee et al. (2025a, 2025b), Papamarkou et al. (2024), Warner et al. (2025), and Phi/Llama references. It briefly distinguishes contextual from non-contextual embedding geometry and positions the work within topological deep learning. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain intact. V2 makes localized language and terminology edits, expands several explanatory paragraphs, adds an appendix contents list, and replaces the preprint footer with conference information.

P2.justification: Appendix C.1 substantially reorganizes its comparative displays: paired half-violins become multiway violin plots, Figure 11 expands, v1 Figures 12–13 are consolidated and expanded into v2 Figure 12, and new Phi/Llama Figures 13–14 are added. Main Figures 3–4 revise axis presentation, and Table 1 gains an ICLR row.

improvement.justification: The larger-model evaluations and additional domain checks strengthen applicability evidence beyond v1's RoBERTa/GPT-2 experiments. Correlation analyses quantify earlier visual observations, and code links improve reproducibility information. More cautious conclusions and an explicit causal limitation improve calibration, although predictive language persists in the abstract and the new correlations do not establish advance prediction. These are useful, bounded improvements to the existing empirical case.
